newsitem.title: USA: Jury making progress in Food Lion case.
newsitem.headline: Jury making progress in Food Lion case.

text.p: A federal jury said it was making progress on Tuesday as it deliberated punitive damages against ABC television for a report alleging Food Lion Inc engaged in unsanitary food handling practices.
For most of its five days of deliberations, the panel had appeared deadlocked but late Tuesday the foreman told U.S. District Judge Carlton Tilley that the jury was making headway.
Tilley allowed jurors to break for the day at 5 p.m. Deliberations were due to resume on Wednesday morning.
After 5 1/2 hours of deliberations Tuesday, the jury sent a note to the judge asking if it could break at 5 p.m. and return to deliberations on Wednesday at 9:30 a.m.
Tilley called jurors into the courtroom to ask a question.
"I'd like to inquire whether or not you're making any progress?" Tilley asked.
The jury foreman answered "Yes, we are -- finally."
Tilley then granted the request, sending the panel back to finish deliberations for the day before breaking until Wednesday.
Several times during its week of deliberations, the jury had sent notes to the judge saying it was stalemated. But Tilley implored the jurors to keep trying.
The jury has spent more than 28 hours weighing evidence in the supermarket chain's fraud lawsuit against ABC.
In 1992, ABC's "PrimeTime Live" broadcast a report that showed pictures of spoiled meat and unsanitary practices at several Food Lion stores.

The Salisbury, N.C.-based company said its sales and stock price plunged after the broadcast, which was based on video obtained by two ABC undercover journalists who wore hidden cameras while briefly working for Food Lion as a deli clerk and meat wrapper.
Food Lion has not challenged the truth of the ABC story, but sued ABC, a unit of Walt Disney Co., and its producers for fraud and trespassing.
Last month, the jury found ABC liable for fraud and ordered the network to pay actual damages of $1,400.
The case is being closely watched by major news organizations, which worry that this represents a new way companies have to attack newsgathering, without filing a libel lawsuit.
Food Lion is a unit of Belgian retailer Ets Delhaize Freres et Cie "LE LION' SA and had 1996 sales of $9 billion.
